claims.text: High configurational entropy stabilizes the atomic arrangement of low–noble-metal, near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles under cyclic high-temperature catalytic conditions.
High configurational entropy prevents surface segregation in these nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy prevents phase separation in these nanoparticles.
Suppression of surface segregation and phase separation preserves catalytic activity.
A Pt-Ni-Cu-Co nanoparticle containing approximately 10 at.% Pt is an example of the proposed near-equiatomic, low–noble-metal initial state.
The proposed initial nanoparticles have a highly disordered atomic structure.
Slight deviations from equiatomic composition reduce configurational entropy relative to an equiatomic baseline.
Atomic randomness and local chemical ordering can be assessed using high-resolution TEM and atom probe tomography.
High configurational entropy creates an energetic barrier to atomic rearrangement.
The proposed energetic barrier lowers the likelihood of surface segregation.
Lower configurational entropy reduces the energetic penalty for local ordering and surface segregation.
Local ordering and surface segregation can compromise nanoparticle structural integrity and catalytic function.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will retain a uniform elemental distribution during exposure at 773–1173 K under alternating oxidizing and reducing atmospheres.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will maintain stable catalytic activity under the specified exposure.
Off-equiatomic nanoparticles will develop localized elemental enrichment or depletion, particularly at their surfaces.
Off-equiatomic nanoparticles will show a measurable decline in catalytic performance over time relative to the equiatomic control.
The equiatomic control is expected to resist surface segregation under the specified conditions.
The hypothesized behavior is limited to low–noble-metal HEA nanoparticles at 773–1173 K under alternating oxidizing and reducing catalytic environments.
Slight composition changes may alter intrinsic catalytic properties independently of configurational entropy.

contradictions.description: The initial-state example describes a four-element Pt-Ni-Cu-Co particle with approximately 10 at.% Pt as near-equiatomic, whereas a strictly equiatomic four-element composition would contain approximately 25 at.% of each element. The actual baseline composition is therefore internally ambiguous.

The intervention changes composition to alter entropy, but the uncertainty field acknowledges that composition also changes intrinsic catalytic properties. The experiment does not provide an independent control that separates configurational entropy from those compositional effects, despite the request for a controlled intervention that distinguishes competing explanations.
